subject: Seller registration, usage tiers & product-page copy — next steps
messages:
From: Sofia Ramos <sofia.ramos@acme-analytics.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@acme-analytics.com>
Date: 2026-08-19T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Seller registration + usage-tiers copy questions

Hi Rachel —

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. We're excited to get Redwood listed on AWS Marketplace and to get the co-sell motion started. A couple of things came up on our side while we collect procurement docs and fill the seller registration: 

- Usage tiers: our billing team would like the public product page to show the three billing tiers (Starter / Scale / Enterprise) with sample monthly unit ranges. Can Redwood confirm whether tier descriptions should be framed as "suggested usage" vs. guaranteed thresholds? We want to avoid wording that implies hard guarantees.

- Conditional pricing / discounts: we plan to offer a 12-month prepay discount for Enterprise. Is that pricing model supported on the Marketplace listing page or should we surface it only in the private contract?

- Badging: AWS requested specific phrasing for the "Data Residency" and "Private Offer" badges. Do you have recommended copy so we match Redwood's policy language?

- Seller registration: please confirm the contact we should use for the AWS seller account and whether Redwood will be the primary listing owner or if Acme will retain ownner-level access. I attached our seller-checklist for reference.

Attachments: acme_seller_checklist.xlsx (xlsx)

Thanks — happy to hop on a short call.

—Sofia
Sofia Ramos
Head of Cloud Partnerships | Acme Analytics
sofia.ramos@acme-analytics.com
+1 (415) 555-0142
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ramos <sofia.ramos@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-19T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Seller registration + usage-tiers copy questions

Hi Sofia — great to hear, and thanks for the checklist. Looping in Vanessa (Marketplace GTM) and Karthik (Legal) — they'll help finalize the public copy and confirm what we can publish versus what needs to stay in the private offer. Ben from Marketplace Ops will run the seller-account/registration flow.

Quick answers to start: 
- Usage tiers: we typically present tiers as "recommended usage ranges" (non-binding) on the public product page and reserve precise SLA/throughput guarantees for the Dedicated/Private deployments in contract language. If you want sample wording, see the draft attached (draft_offer_page_v0.md).

- Conditional pricing: AWS Marketplace supports private offers and custom pricing for negotiated deals; public listing does not typically show conditional prepay discounts. We can surface a note on the product page saying "Contact us for Enterprise pricing and prepay discounts" and include a link to a private offer / procurement contact.

- Badging: Karthik — can you confirm the short badge copy we should use for Data Residency and Private Offer?

Next steps: Ben, can you confirm the recommended primary listing owner flows (Redwood vs. Acme) and any docs we need filled out on your side?

Attachments: draft_offer_page_v0.md (md)

Thanks — Rachel
Rachel Kim
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.com
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-19T16:32:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Seller registration + usage-tiers copy questions

On Thu, Aug 19, 2026 at 11:05 AM Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com> wrote:
> Quick answers to start: 
> - Usage tiers: we typically present tiers as "recommended usage ranges" (non-binding) on the public product page and reserve precise SLA/throughput guarantees for the Dedicated/Private deployments in contract language.

Agree with Rachel. A few legal notes to avoid procurement friction: 
1) Public copy must not include contractual language (e.g., "guarantee", "commitment", or explicit performance numbers). Use phrasing like "typical monthly usage" or "recommended for...".
2) For prepay discounts: call it a "Private Offer / Negotiated Discount" on the listing. Avoid listing discount percentages on the public page.
3) Data residency badge: recommended short copy — "Data residency options available (US/EU) — contact sales for details". We should ensure that any storage/retention language links back to our security & compliance page.
4) Marketplace badging: include an explicit line that "Private Offer participation is subject to a separate agreement."

I'll add the required legal boilerplate and return a marked-up draft by EOD. If procurement needs a registrant email for seller-account access, recommend using marketplace-ops@redwood.com (managed mailbox).

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-20T09:00:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Seller registration + usage-tiers copy questions — ops steps

Rachel / team —

Thanks. Quick ops breakdown for AWS seller registration and listing publication: 
1) Owner model: Redwood can be the primary listing owner (recommended for faster updates and co-sell ops). If Acme requires owner-level permissions we can set up delegated admin access; that adds an extra review step in AWS (usually 2 business days).
2) Required docs: W-9 (US sellers) or equivalent tax docs, bank ACH info for payouts, and DSAR contact for compliance.
3) Steps we will run: enroll Redwood as co-sell partner in your HubSpot deal, create the product listing draft in AWS account, attach the S3 bundle, open the private offer workspace if needed.
4) Timeline: from signed seller registration to live listing typically 7-10 business days if we have all docs.

I attached a step-by-step PDF (aws_seller_steps.pdf) that we can share with Acme procurement. Ben from Marketplace Ops will be the day-to-day contact: ben.carter@redwood.com.

Attachments: aws_seller_steps.pdf (pdf)

—Ben
Ben Carter
Marketplace Operations, Redwood Inference

Date: 2026-08-22T08:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Seller registration + usage-tiers copy questions — agreed copy & next steps

Sofia / Acme procurement —

Thanks for the fast turnaround. Per the internal review, here is what we agreed and next steps to keep things moving: 

1) Public listing copy: we will publish tier labels and recommended usage ranges only (non-binding). See attached final_offer_page_copy_v1.docx for the exact phrasing. Public call-to-action will read: "Contact us for Enterprise pricing and private-offer discounts."

2) Badges: use the concise badge text: 
   - "Data residency options (US / EU) — contact sales for details"
   - "Private Offer available — subject to separate agreement"

3) Conditional pricing: Enterprise prepay discounts will be executed via Private Offer / negotiated contract. We'll not publish discount percentages on the public page.

4) Seller registration: Redwood recommends Redwood be the primary listing owner for faster updates. If Acme requires owner access, we will set up delegated admin (2 business day AWS review). Please return the completed seller registration form we filled in with Acme's bank info. I'm attaching a filled copy for your convenience.

5) Timeline & MP support: Once we have the filled registration + W-9, Ben will start the listing draft. Expected publish window 7-10 business days.

Action items: 
- Sofia / Procurement: sign and return seller_registration_form_filled.pdf; provide W-9 and bank details.
- Acme: confirm whether you want Redwood as primary owner or delegated admin.
- Redwood: Ben to open listing draft and Karthik to finalize short legal boilerplate on the product page.

Mutual action plan link: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/7894

Attachments: final_offer_page_copy_v1.docx (docx), seller_registration_form_filled.pdf (pdf)
